subject: MAP: Data classification & retention acceptance criteria — FinLane pilot
messages:
From: Ava Patel <ava.p@finlane.io>
To: soojin_lee@redwoodai.com
Cc: Will Gomez <will.gomez@finlane.io>
Date: 2026-10-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff: data classification & retention acceptance criteria for pilot

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited to kick off the pilot. Before we lock dates, our security team needs a clear MAP section for the security/compliance gates that will be required for final acceptance. Specifically we need:

- A mapping of SOC 2 in-scope controls you will authoritatively provide evidence for during the pilot (Type II not required for pilot, but evidence of control operation requested)
- Completed SIG/CAIQ responses or a clear list of gaps and remediation timelines
- A proposed DPA retention schedule for: production hosted API, dedicated deployment, and EU-region data handling
- Clarification on log retention (request/response payloads, KV cache logs, debug traces) and whether these can be shortened for EU traffic

Can you send an initial MAP subsection we can circulate to our security lead? We’d like to keep the pilot go/no-go decision window to 4 weeks from start, so timing is tight.

Appreciate it — attaching the pilot statement of work for reference.

Regards,
Ava
Ava Patel
Security Program Manager
FinLane, Inc.
Attachment: FinLane-Pilot-SOW.pdf (application/pdf)

------------------------------------------------------------

From: soojin_lee@redwoodai.com
To: Ava Patel <ava.p@finlane.io>
Cc: Will Gomez <will.gomez@finlane.io>, kimberly_park@redwoodai.com
Date: 2026-10-23T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: data classification & retention acceptance criteria for pilot

Ava — thanks for the clear list. Draft MAP subsection attached (MAP-draft-FinLane.xlsx) and a short CAIQ gap summary (CAIQ-gap-report.pdf). High-level summary below so your security lead can scan quickly.

1) Data classification (pilot scope)
   - Personal Data (PD): customer-identifying info supplied in prompts (names, emails, account ids).
   - Pseudonymized Data: tokenized identifiers / hashed ids used by your app.
   - System/Operational Logs: API access logs, latency metrics, anonymized inference traces (sampling enabled).

2) Proposed retention windows (default / pilot-specific)
   - Hosted API (standard): PD retained for 30 days for debugging and quality checks, pseudonymized data 90 days, logs 180 days.
   - Dedicated deployment (reserved infra): PD retention configurable by customer; default 30 days; can set 7/30/90 day windows during onboarding.
   - EU-region traffic: default PD retention shortened to 14 days on request; must be enabled prior to pilot start to ensure region routing and legal config.

3) SOC 2 / evidence plan
   - We will provide mapped artifacts for the following control families during pilot: CC6 (system operations), CC7 (change management), CC8 (logical access), CC9 (system monitoring). Evidence types: architecture diagrams, firewall/access lists, config snapshots, and weekly incident logs.
   - For pilot acceptance we ask for evidence review rather than a completed Type II report. If Type II required for production, we’ll include that as a post-pilot deliverable.

4) SIG/CAIQ status and remediation timeline
   - Attached: CAIQ-gap-report.pdf highlighting 6 items with recommended remediation windows (2–6 weeks depending on scope).
   - We propose to deliver updated CAIQ answers and remediation evidence by Week 3 of the pilot for any medium-severity gaps.

5) DPA & retention clauses
   - We will propose the same DPA language we use with other fintechs; the pilot DPA will include retention schedules and an option for EU short-retain. Kimberly (legal) is on cc to handle redlines.

6) Acceptance gates (mutual) — acceptance checklist for go/no-go
   - Security acceptance review completed (review of provided evidence + CAIQ answers)
   - DPA signed or exchanged with mutually agreed retention window
   - No outstanding critical gaps flagged by FinLane security (medium gaps must have remediation plan <= 6 weeks)

7) Timeline (proposed)
   - Week 0: Pilot start / configuration (enable EU short retention if requested)
   - Week 1: SOC evidence package delivered for review; CAIQ updated initial answers
   - Week 2: Security Q&A and remediation begins
   - Week 3: Updated CAIQ + remediation evidence; DPA redline exchange
   - Week 4: Final acceptance decision (go/no-go)

Next steps — can we confirm whether your security lead needs additional artifacts (e.g., KMS key rotation policy, HSM usage)? If we get confirmation today, we can lock pilot start for 2026-11-08 and maintain the 4-week acceptance window.

Thanks — attaching the spreadsheet and CAIQ summary.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Security Programs | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwoodai.com
Attachment: MAP-draft-FinLane.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
Attachment: CAIQ-gap-report.pdf (application/pdf)

------------------------------------------------------------

From: Will Gomez <will.gomez@finlane.io>
To: soojin_lee@redwoodai.com
Cc: Ava Patel <ava.p@finlane.io>
Date: 2026-10-24T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: data classification & retention acceptance criteria for pilot

Thanks, Soojin — this is helpful. A couple clarifying Qs from our side:

- When you say "PD retained for 30 days for debugging", does that include full request/response payloads (we typically want to avoid storing unredacted payloads)? Can you confirm if Redwood supports automatic prompt redaction or masking for hosted API?
- For the EU short-retain option (14 days), would the logs/metrics still be retained 180 days as you mentioned, or can that be aligned to 30/14 as well? We need a clear split: payload retention vs telemetry/log retention.
- KMS handling: do you provide a customer-managed KMS option for Dedicated or Private deployments? If so, does the pilot need a separate onboarding window to provision keys?

Inline: 
> 
> 3) SOC 2 / evidence plan
>   - We will provide mapped artifacts for the following control families during pilot: CC6, CC7, CC8, CC9.

If your team can flag exact artifact names we can circulate to our auditor (e.g., config snapshot file names, expected log sample names).

Will
Will Gomez
Head of Platform Security
FinLane

------------------------------------------------------------

From: kimberly_park@redwoodai.com
To: Will Gomez <will.gomez@finlane.io>, Ava Patel <ava.p@finlane.io>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwoodai.com, ben_carter@redwoodai.com
Date: 2026-10-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: data classification & retention acceptance criteria for pilot

Hi Will / Ava — looping in legal. Quick answers and next steps:

- Payload retention: Hosted API can be configured to store full request/response payloads for debugging; default is 30 days. We also provide a prompt redaction feature (configurable per-customer) that strips configured fields before storage. We recommend enabling redaction for PD fields during the pilot.
- Telemetry/logs: Telemetry (metrics/aggregated traces) retained 180 days by default for Hosted; we can shorten to 30 days for EU-only telemetry on request. Full raw debug traces (if enabled) are treated as operational logs and follow the log retention policy; we can scope sampling and retention per region but need to capture that in the DPA exhibit.
- KMS: Customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers can opt for tenant-specific keys with integration to our KMS provider — we will document the onboarding steps. Dedicated/private will require key exchange and a 3–5 business day provisioning window; plan for that in Week 0 if required.

Attached: DPA-redline.docx (minor retention exhibit edits and an optional EU short-retain clause). Please review and return via DocuSign link below.

DocuSign (draft): https://docusign.com/pa/embeddedSigning?txn=0x9a3f-finlane-DPA

Kimberly Park
